concepts.title: Supervised Learning Basics
keyPoints: Fit f(x) → y from labeled (input, output) pairs
Regression = continuous y (squared error); classification = categorical y (cross-entropy)
Training = ERM: minimize (1/n) Σ L(f(x_i), y_i) on training data
Overfitting: H too flexible for n — regularize, simplify, or add data
Leakage/train-serve skew is the real production killer, not model choice

concepts.title: Bias-Variance Tradeoff
keyPoints: Test error = Bias² + Variance + irreducible noise (σ²)
Bias = systematic error from a too-simple model class (underfit)
Variance = sensitivity of predictions to the training sample (overfit)
More data shrinks variance only — bias needs more capacity/features
Diagnose which regime via train/validation gap, not one error number

concepts.title: Categorical Encoding
keyPoints: Converts categorical variables into numeric form models can consume
Ordinal encoding: compact but implies false order/distance for nominal data
One-hot encoding: safe default under ~20–50 categories; else sparse blowup
Target (mean) encoding: smoothed per-category target stat, standard for high-cardinality GBMs
Leakage gotcha: encode out-of-fold only, fallback to global mean for unseen categories

concepts.title: Confusion Matrix
keyPoints: Cross-tabulates predicted vs true labels: TP, FP, FN, TN counts
Every metric (accuracy, precision, recall, F1) is arithmetic on these four cells
Multi-class: N×N grid, diagonal = correct, cell [i,j] = predicted j when truth i
Exposes failures accuracy hides — e.g. 99.9% accuracy but recall = 0 on rare fraud class
Gotcha: recall normalizes over rows, precision over columns — check label order, don't assume [0,0] is TP

concepts.title: Feature Scaling
keyPoints: Puts numeric features on a shared scale before distance/gradient/regularization steps
Standardization: z = (x − μ) / σ — zero mean, unit variance
Min-max: x' = (x − min) / (max − min) — compresses to [0, 1]
Unscaled features stretch the loss surface, causing gradient descent to zig-zag
Fit scaler on train fold only, then transform val/test — avoids data leakage

concepts.title: Linear Regression
keyPoints: Fits y ≈ Xw + b by minimizing sum of squared errors
Normal equation: w = (XᵀX)⁻¹Xᵀy — exact but O(p³), fails if singular
Gradient descent scales to large n/p and is required for L1 (Lasso)
Weights are directly interpretable (e.g. '$150 per sqft')
Check residual plots — curve = nonlinearity, funnel = heteroscedasticity, not caught by R²

concepts.title: Naive Bayes
keyPoints: Generative classifier: Bayes' rule + conditional independence given class
P(x|y) = ∏ᵢ P(xᵢ|y) — turns 1 hard n-D problem into n easy 1-D ones
Fit in one pass: counts (Multinomial), presence (Bernoulli), or mean/var (Gaussian)
Predict via argmax of log P(y) + Σ log P(xᵢ|y), to avoid underflow
Zero-frequency gotcha: unseen feature zeroes whole product — fix with Laplace smoothing

concepts.title: Accuracy and Class Imbalance
keyPoints: Accuracy = (TP+TN)/(TP+TN+FP+FN) — misleading under class imbalance
Trivial 'always predict majority class' model scores high accuracy, 0% recall
Accuracy paradox: 1% fraud rate → predicting 'no fraud' always = 99% accuracy
Gotcha: catching more of the rare class often lowers accuracy (more false positives)
Fix: use per-class recall/precision/F1, PR-AUC, or balanced accuracy instead

concepts.title: Cross-Validation
keyPoints: Resampling procedure estimating generalization error via repeated splits
K-fold: train on k−1 folds, validate on held-out, rotate, average
k=5/10 standard: balances bias (small k) vs variance/cost (LOOCV)
Leakage gotcha: fit scalers/encoders only on training fold, via Pipeline
Grouped or time-ordered data: use GroupKFold/TimeSeriesSplit, not random folds

concepts.title: Decision Trees
keyPoints: Recursively partitions feature space via axis-aligned if/else splits
Each split greedily minimizes Gini/entropy (classification) or variance (regression)
Recurses until max depth, min leaf size, or no impurity gain
Greedy, no lookahead — locally best split can block a better tree
Unconstrained trees overfit (high variance) — prune or ensemble via bagging/boosting

concepts.title: Gradient Descent
keyPoints: Iteratively updates θ := θ − α∇J(θ) to minimize a loss function
Trades closed-form exactness for cheap iteration on hard/huge problems
Learning rate α too large → oscillate/diverge; too small → crawl
Unscaled features stretch the loss bowl into an ellipse → zig-zag
Fix is standardizing features, not shrinking α — Adam/momentum also compensate

concepts.title: K-Means Clustering
keyPoints: Unsupervised: partitions n points into k clusters via nearest centroid
Lloyd's algorithm: assign to nearest centroid, update centroid = mean, repeat
Each iteration never increases inertia, so it's guaranteed to converge
Only reaches a local optimum — bad init can permanently strand centroids
Fix: k-means++ distance-weighted seeding, plus always standardize features first

concepts.title: k-Nearest Neighbors
keyPoints: Lazy learning: no training, just stores data
Predict = majority vote (or mean) of k closest points
k controls bias-variance: k=1 low bias/high variance, large k smooths
Must standardize features — unscaled distance is dominated by large-range features
High dimensions: distances concentrate, hurting raw k-NN over many features

concepts.title: L1 and L2 Regularization
keyPoints: Adds penalty term to loss: L1 = Σ|w|, L2 = Σw²
L2 shrinks all weights smoothly (closed form: (XᵀX+λI)⁻¹Xᵀy)
L1's corner-shaped constraint region drives weights to exactly zero
L1 → sparse/interpretable models; L2 → correlated features, stability
Must standardize features first — penalty is scale-sensitive

concepts.title: Precision and Recall
keyPoints: Precision = TP/(TP+FP): of predicted positives, how many are right
Recall = TP/(TP+FN): of actual positives, how many were caught
Both read the same confusion matrix, different row/column
Sliding the classification threshold trades one for the other
Report both at a named threshold — either alone can be gamed

concepts.title: Principal Component Analysis
keyPoints: Projects data onto orthogonal directions of max variance (covariance eigenvectors)
Rank components by eigenvalue = variance explained, keep top-k
Computed via SVD of centered X (avoids forming covariance matrix directly)
Requires standardized features — PCA isn't scale-invariant, large-range features dominate
Trades interpretability for compression; only captures linear structure

concepts.title: Data Leakage
keyPoints: Info unavailable at inference time leaks into training
Corrupts the validation signal itself, not just the model
Preprocessing leakage: fit scaler/PCA on full data before split
Fix: wrap transforms in a Pipeline, refit per CV fold
Target leakage: feature is causally downstream of the label

concepts.title: Decision Threshold
keyPoints: Cutoff t: predict positive when score s(x) ≥ t
Chosen after training — tunable with zero retraining
Sweeping t from 0→1 traces the model's ROC/PR curve
Raising t buys precision, costs recall (fewer, surer positives)
Gotcha: fixed-t precision drifts if serving-time class balance shifts

concepts.title: F1 Score
keyPoints: F1 = 2·precision·recall / (precision + recall), the harmonic mean
Harmonic mean punishes imbalance: P=1.0, R=0 gives F1=0, not 0.5
Default single-metric summary for imbalanced binary classification
Assumes FP and FN cost the same — rarely true in production
Use F-beta instead: beta>1 weights recall, beta<1 weights precision

concepts.title: Gradient Boosting
keyPoints: Sequentially fits trees to the negative gradient of the loss
Functional gradient descent — adds a shrunk tree each round: F += lr·h_m(X)
Reduces bias (vs. bagging/Random Forest, which reduces variance via parallel averaging)
'Residual fitting' is just the squared-error special case, not the general rule
Sequential dependency (F_m needs F_{m-1}) blocks cross-tree parallelism, unlike Random Forest

concepts.title: Logistic Regression
keyPoints: Models log-odds as w·x+b; sigmoid converts it to a probability
Sigmoid isn't arbitrary — it's forced by the log-odds linearity assumption
Trained by minimizing cross-entropy loss instead of squared error
Gradient reduces to (p−y)·x — same form as linear regression's
Separable data → unregularized MLE diverges; production models always regularize

concepts.title: Random Forests
keyPoints: Ensemble of trees on bootstrapped rows + random feature subsets, then vote/average
Each split considers only a random feature subset (√p classification, p/3 regression)
Goal is decorrelating trees — variance floor is ρσ², not zero
~36.8% out-of-bag rows per tree give free validation, no holdout needed
Default impurity feature importance is biased; prefer permutation importance or SHAP

concepts.title: ROC and PR Curves
keyPoints: Sweep the classifier's decision threshold over scored predictions
ROC: FPR (x) vs TPR/Recall (y); PR: Recall (x) vs Precision (y)
Precision's denominator (predicted positives) is tiny vs FPR's (all negatives)
Under imbalance, ROC-AUC can look great while PR-AUC exposes noise
No-skill baseline: ROC-AUC=0.5 always; PR-AUC = positive prevalence

concepts.title: Calibration
keyPoints: Predicted probabilities match true empirical frequency of outcome
Orthogonal to discrimination — AUC=1 possible while probabilities are garbage
Single trees overconfident (pure leaves); bagged forests underconfident (averaging shrinks to 0.5)
Fix post-hoc: Platt scaling or isotonic regression on held-out data
Both are monotonic — fix values, not ranking; never fit on training data

concepts.title: Cross-Entropy Loss
keyPoints: Negative log-likelihood of the true class: L = -Σ y_k·log(ŷ_k)
One-hot y ⇒ collapses to L = -log(ŷ_correct)
Loss explodes toward ∞ as predicted p→0 for the true class
Paired with softmax, gradient w.r.t. logits simplifies to ŷ - y
MSE+sigmoid reintroduces σ'(z)≈0 when confidently wrong — vanishing gradient

concepts.title: Neural Networks (MLP)
keyPoints: Stacks affine layers (Wx+b) each followed by a nonlinearity
Nonlinearity between layers lets it bend space into non-linear boundaries
Trained via backpropagation: chain rule propagates gradients through every layer
Without nonlinearity, layers collapse algebraically into one linear model (can't solve XOR)
Deep sigmoid/tanh stacks vanish gradients — fix with ReLU, He/Xavier init, normalization

concepts.title: Support Vector Machines
keyPoints: Max-margin linear classifier: widest separating hyperplane, margin = 2/‖w‖
Soft margin adds slack ξᵢ + penalty C for non-separable data
Sparse solution: only support vectors (on/inside margin) set the boundary
Kernel trick: swap dot products for K(x,z) (e.g., RBF) for nonlinear boundaries
Must feature-scale first — margin/RBF distance is scale-sensitive

concepts.title: Activation Functions
keyPoints: Nonlinear elementwise transform on Wx+b after each layer
Without it, stacked linear layers collapse to one linear map
Sigmoid/tanh saturate → derivative ≤0.25, vanishes geometrically with depth
ReLU derivative=1 for positive inputs → enables deep training
Gotcha: dead ReLUs (stuck negative) or Xavier init mismatched with ReLU

concepts.title: Backpropagation
keyPoints: Reverse-mode autodiff: chain rule backward through the computational graph
Forward pass caches activations; backward pass reuses them for dL/dθ
Per layer: δ_prev = Wᵀ(δ ⊙ g'(z)) — only needs local cache + incoming δ
Cost ≈ one extra forward pass total, not per parameter — this is the whole point
Gotchas: vanishing/exploding gradients (depth compounding); memory (not compute) binds, hence checkpointing

concepts.title: Neural Network Regularization
keyPoints: Nets are overparameterized — weight penalties alone don't stop memorization
Dropout: zero fraction p of activations, scale survivors by 1/(1-p)
BatchNorm/LayerNorm smooth the loss landscape, incidentally regularizing
Early stopping caps gradient steps; augmentation enlarges effective data
AdamW decouples weight decay from grad scaling — Adam's L2 doesn't

concepts.title: Normalization (Batch and Layer)
keyPoints: Standardize pre-activations to zero mean/unit variance, then learned affine y = γx̂ + β
BatchNorm reduces over the batch (+ spatial dims), per feature
LayerNorm reduces over the feature dim, per individual example
BatchNorm needs frozen running mean/var at inference (train/eval mode); LayerNorm has none
CNNs default to BatchNorm; Transformers/LLMs default to LayerNorm/RMSNorm (variable length, batch-size-1 decoding)

concepts.title: Optimizers (SGD, Momentum, Adam)
keyPoints: Optimizer turns a loss gradient into a parameter update each step
SGD steps directly opposite the mini-batch gradient, scaled by a fixed LR
Momentum: EMA of past gradients (velocity) cancels oscillation, speeds consistent progress
Adam: bias-corrected 1st & 2nd moment give each parameter its own adaptive step size
Gotcha: momentum's effective step ≈ lr/(1−β); Adam needs LR warmup + gradient clipping

concepts.title: Self-Attention
keyPoints: Each token: weighted average of all tokens' value vectors
Weights = softmax(QK^T) — content-based, not fixed by position
Q=what I seek, K=what I offer, V=what I give if attended
Divide by sqrt(d_k): keeps dot-product variance at 1, avoids softmax saturation
Causal mask: set future scores to -inf before softmax, not after

concepts.title: Vanishing and Exploding Gradients
keyPoints: Backprop gradient = chain-rule product of per-layer Jacobians
Factors consistently <1 vanish exponentially; >1 explode exponentially with depth
Sigmoid derivative maxes at 0.25 → 20 layers ≈ dead gradient; ReLU (deriv=1) fixes this
RNNs: gradient scales as W_hh^T — spectral radius <1 vanishes, >1 explodes over timesteps
Same mechanism both directions — fix via normalization, residual connections, gradient clipping, not just bigger init
